# `m.stocks.filings.disclosures_8k`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Disclosures in 8-K current reports, classified by category, one row per disclosure.

```python
m.stocks.filings.disclosures_8k(symbols=None, *, start=None, end=None, sort=None, order=None, limit=None, filters=None)
```

[All datasets](README.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Verbs | `fetch()`, `poll()` |
| Served by | REST |
| Time range | `start` and `end` are sent as `filing_date.gte` and `filing_date.lte` |
| `poll()` | `dm.PollMode.APPEND`: appends only rows it has not seen, keyed by `AccessionNumber`, `PrimaryCategory`, `SecondaryCategory`, `TertiaryCategory`, `SupportingText` and `Symbol` |
| `sort` | any REST field of the rows (see Massive fields below), or several separated by commas, each with an optional `.asc` or `.desc` |
| `filters` | `cik`, `cik_any_of`, `tertiary_category` |

## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `symbols` | Tickers whose filings to return; None, the default, for every filing. | Massive's ticker for each symbol, spelled exactly as Massive spells it: `AAPL` or `BRK.B` for a stock, `O:SPY271217C00700000` (the OCC code) for an option, `I:SPX` for an index, `C:EURUSD` for a forex pair, `X:BTCUSD` for a crypto pair, and `ESZ6` for a future. Pass one symbol as text, several as a list, or a table with a `Symbol` column. A live table is followed: each symbol you add is read, and each one you delete stops being read. `last_by()`, `fetch()`, `history()`, and most polls also drop a deleted symbol's rows. `dm.ALL` reads every symbol, and leaving the argument out reads every record with no filter by symbol, where this dataset takes them. A misspelled symbol in text or a list raises `ValueError` at the call; by default, a misspelled row of a table is skipped and logged, and the table keeps running. `dm.canonical_symbol` converts other spellings to Massive's. A record that lists several symbols, such as a news article, appears once for each symbol you named that it lists. |
| `start` | The first filing date. | The first day or moment of the range. A date (text such as `"2025-06-02"`, a Python `date`, or a Deephaven `LocalDate`) means the day in the market's time zone: New York for stocks, options, and indices; UTC for forex and crypto; for futures, the trading session that ends that day. An instant is an exact time: a Python `datetime` with a time zone, a `pandas.Timestamp`, a `numpy.datetime64`, a Deephaven `Instant` or `ZonedDateTime`, or Deephaven time text such as `"2025-06-02T09:30 ET"`. Give `start` and `end` as two dates or two instants. A `datetime` without a time zone raises `ValueError`, and a calendar-date field, such as an ex-dividend date, takes dates only. |
| `end` | The last filing date. | The last day, or the moment the range stops, in the same form as `start`. A date includes its whole day, so `start="2025-06-02", end="2025-06-02"` reads all of June 2; an instant is excluded. Leave it out to read through now; a list dataset then sends Massive no end, so it also returns records still to come, such as dividends announced but not yet paid. |
| `sort` | The field to sort by, such as `"filing_date"`. | The field to order the rows by, named as Massive names it, such as `"ex_dividend_date"`. Where the endpoint allows, name several, separated by commas, each with an optional `.asc` or `.desc`: `"ticker,ex_dividend_date.desc"`. This page lists the values the dataset takes. |
| `order` | The direction of `sort`. | The direction of `sort`: `dm.Order.ASC` or `dm.Order.DESC`. |
| `limit` | The most rows to return, in total. | The most rows Massive returns for the whole request, across every symbol you name, kept in Massive's order: ask for newest first (`order=dm.Order.DESC`) to keep the latest. A symbol that comes first can use up the whole limit, so leave `limit` out when you need every row of each symbol. A `fetch()` that follows a table of symbols applies it to each symbol's request, and this dataset's own line says where else it applies to each symbol. |
| `filters` | Further endpoint parameters, such as `{"tertiary_category": "Dividends"}`. | Any other parameter Massive documents for this dataset, as a mapping from the parameter's name to its value, with each dot in the name written as `_`: Massive's `strike_price.gte` is `strike_price_gte`. This page lists the keys the dataset takes. A key it doesn't take, or one that has its own argument, such as `start`, raises `ValueError` naming the keys it does take. A date or time value takes ISO 8601 text, or any value `start` takes. |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The ticker the request named that the row lists in `Tickers`: a row that lists several of the named tickers appears once for each, so an article about AAPL and MSFT read for both is listed under each. A request that named one ticker gives it to every row. Null when the call named no ticker, and on a row that lists none of a request's named tickers. | REST |
| `AccessionNumber` | String | Unique SEC accession number for the filing (e.g., '0000320193-25-000010'). | REST |
| `Cik` | String | SEC Central Index Key of the filer (10 digits, zero-padded). | REST |
| `FilingDate` | String | Date when the filing was submitted to the SEC (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD). | REST |
| `FilingUrl` | String | Direct URL to the full submission text file for the filing on SEC EDGAR. | REST |
| `PrimaryCategory` | String | Top-level disclosure category (e.g., 'financial_results'). See the full taxonomy at /stocks/taxonomies/vX/disclosures. | REST |
| `SecondaryCategory` | String | Mid-level disclosure category (e.g., 'earnings_announcement'). See the full taxonomy at /stocks/taxonomies/vX/disclosures. | REST |
| `SupportingText` | String | A verbatim excerpt from the filing text supporting the assigned categories. | REST |
| `TertiaryCategory` | String | Most specific disclosure category (e.g., 'quarterly_results'). Filtering on this column must use an exact match. See the full taxonomy at /stocks/taxonomies/vX/disclosures. | REST |
| `Tickers` | String[] | A list of ticker symbols for the filing company. Multiple symbols may indicate different share classes; empty if no ticker is currently mapped to the filer. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
